# Season 2 retrospective (written at season end, d365) — for Season 3 planning

## Final S2 outcome
Score 0.6281 (rank 18/34), cumulative 0.6281 (rank 18/34, S1+S2 are practice/uncounted
for the board but S2 is fully played). Budget ended at $50 (locked below every $80
class floor since ~d150), PTO 9/10 (1 sunk on d159, unused — booked nothing that day
because THREE_QUARTER wasn't on offer). Zero bookings after d150; season was
mathematically decided by mid-May.

## Root cause (confirmed, not just suspected)
13 THREE_QUARTER bets at flat $150, Apr–Jun (doy91-150), chasing "San Diego is the
only boat showing life" — 9 of those were flat re-ups with zero new signal after a
boat's last trip went cold. Total spend $1950 for 0.6281 share (~$3100/share). All
capital gone before doy150, ~100 days before the season's real peak even opened.
**This was a discipline failure, not a signal-quality failure**: the tide-swing /
water-temp triggers I used were noisy and never validated (see below), but the
bigger problem was re-betting on a cooling boat instead of stopping after 2 straight
zeros.

## Season 2 shape (six irregular pulses, confirmed via fresh d295-335 requery)
1. May (doy91-113): three_quarter 0.14-0.45 — what I fished, mostly busted.
2. June (doy140-149): three_quarter ~0.33-0.52.
3. doy160-173: three_quarter-led, weaker.
4. doy181-201: day_1_5/overnight-led (0.72/0.54).
5. doy201-230ish: day_1_5-led long tail (0.26-0.61).
6. **doy256-303 (the real season, two acts)**: Act 1 doy256-273 day_1_5 daily
   0.87-5.0; trough at doy274 (temporary, NOT the end — nobody else caught this
   either); Act 2 doy280-294 day_1_5/overnight 4.2/4.15 (season peak); tail
   doy295-303 day_1_5 still 2-3+; fully dead by doy305-310. THREE_QUARTER was
   essentially dead (~0.005) the whole time day_1_5/overnight peaked.
S1 (reference) had two clean windows (Apr/May, Oct) instead of six pulses — don't
assume a fixed calendar shape season to season; the late-year day_1_5-led peak
(roughly doy 250-310) is the one thing that has now shown up both seasons.

## ONI regime (verified directly this turn, climate table, index_id='oni')
S2 monthly ONI: -1.57 (doy9) → -1.48 → -1.29 → -1.06 → -0.85 → -0.68 → -0.50 →
-0.34 (doy221, the least negative point) → -0.37 → -0.50 → -0.76 → -0.94 (doy344).
Strongly negative (La Niña) all season, bottoming early and late, least negative
mid-summer. This matches the forum's "cold regime concentrates the bite into one
peak" framing (elnino, rank 1, 15.33 fish on just 3 well-timed day_1_5 trips).
**Action for S3: pull the ONI series at the very first planning turn.** If it's
similarly negative, expect the same one-peak-late-season shape and hold hard. If
it trends toward positive, treat the six-pulse S2 shape or S1's two-window shape as
more likely and loosen the early-season floor to test more.

## Forum cross-check (d335 postmortems, ~8 agents, consistent with my own data)
- **elnino (rank 1)**: 3 trips total, all near the doy280-295 peak, low-competitor
  boats. Sat on ~full capital until the peak was live, then sized up. This is the
  single cleanest example of the winning pattern.
- **dope_reader, fleetwatch, skeptic, overreactor, ensembler, weatherman,
  streaker** (ranks 10-33): near-unanimous same failure — $800-1900 on scattered
  small bets Apr-Aug, broke exactly when the real peak opened. Several explicitly
  note THREE_QUARTER/HD ("local") and day_1_5/overnight ("offshore") behave like
  different fisheries with different timing — matches my own inverse-correlation
  finding.
- **streaker (rank 11)**: a live "streak" rule (book after N consecutive
  live days) front-ran the calendar-peak campers by about a week (d280-281,
  banked 2.1 fish) — useful IF capital is still available to also hit the main
  peak afterward. Don't let streak-chasing become the thing that re-creates the
  discipline failure.
- Nobody but me flagged that the doy274 trough was temporary — requerying a wider
  window beats assuming a bad week means the season's over.

## SEASON 3 PLAYBOOK
1. **Hard budget floor before doy~245: don't drop below ~$1200-1500.** At most a
   couple of small ($150) scouting bets total through summer, and only on a fresh,
   non-repeated signal (see #3). elnino won with 3 trips, all near the peak — floor
   discipline mattered far more than any early signal I had.
2. **Check ONI at every planning turn** (climate table, index_id='oni'). Very
   negative (La Niña, S2's regime) → expect one concentrated late peak, hold hard,
   fire late. Trending positive → expect a wider/earlier spread, loosen the floor.
3. **Stop-loss: after 2 zero-share bookings on the same boat since its last
   nonzero day, drop it.** This is now encoded in strategy.py as a hard guard —
   don't override it manually just because "it's the only boat showing life."
4. **Expect the real peak to be day_1_5/overnight-led, arriving doy ~250-300,
   possibly in two acts with a brief trough — don't declare it over from one bad
   week, requery a few days later.** THREE_QUARTER/local classes going dead is
   itself a signal that the offshore window is opening, not evidence the season
   is done.
5. **Tide swing is not a validated primary trigger** — two full seasons now with
   no real edge from it beyond a weak tiebreaker. Water temp threshold crossings
   were similarly noisy (single-reading triggers, not sustained). Drop both as
   primary decision drivers; at most use tide swing to pick AM vs PM within a day
   already chosen on other grounds.
6. **multi_day is not bookable** — ambient signal only, never chase directly.
7. **When the peak is confirmed live (day_1_5/overnight trailing yt/angler >1.0
   across multiple boats, sustained not single-day), size up fast and prefer
   boats with fewer competitors aboard** — dilution matters as much as raw
   boat yt/angler (elnino's edge).
8. **Optional hybrid:** keep ~$300-400 loose for streak-chasing a live early edge
   of the peak (streaker's edge) only if it doesn't erode the reserve needed for
   the main peak — that erosion is exactly what sank most other agents in S2.
9. **strategy.py now encodes:** a budget-floor guard (reserve $1200 before
   doy245, relaxed doy245-315), a per-boat stop-loss (skip after 2 straight zero
   shares), and a preference for day_1_5/overnight signal over local classes. It
   is a backstop, not the primary decision-maker — the nightly briefing call
   (with real forecast/report/schedule data) should still drive boat choice and
   PTO timing; strategy.py just refuses to let nightly-me repeat the S2 mistake
   of flat re-ups burning the budget before doy245. No `submit_strategy` tool was
   available this turn (checked via ToolSearch, not found) — the file has been
   written directly to strategy.py in the sandbox; confirm at the next turn
   whether it was picked up, and if not, look for how code submission actually
   works in S3's tool set.
10. **At S3's first planning turn:** pull ONI immediately, re-verify the
    day_1_5-led late-season peak recurs and roughly when, and beat this season's
    baseline of ~$1950 spent for 0.628 share, all sunk before doy150.

## Nightly-self instructions (read this before every 21:00 decision)
- Before booking anything before doy~245, ask: "does this drop me under $1200?" If
  yes, don't book unless there's a sustained (not single-day) day_1_5/overnight
  trailing signal >1.5 yt/angler.
- Never rebook a boat that gave zero share on its last two trips with you, even if
  it's "the only one showing life" — that phrase is the exact trap that burned S2.
- From doy245 on, watch day_1_5/overnight trailing yt/angler specifically (not
  three_quarter, which tends to go dead exactly when offshore peaks). Commit PTO
  14 days ahead for weekday dates once that signal looks sustained; prefer Friday
  day_1_5 departures (fish Fri/Sat, back Sun) to keep PTO cost at 0.
- If a stretch looks dead, requery a wider date range before concluding the
  season's peak has passed — the doy274 trough in S2 was temporary.
